clue.text: One usually has a second helping

definitions.text: One usually has a second helping

parts.words: One usually has a second helping
parts.note: reads like a greedy diner going back for more food, but the second here is the friend who assists at a formal fight with pistols or swords

explanation.walkthrough: A 'second' is the attendant who supports a fighter in an affair of honour, so 'second helping' means a second who helps.
explanation.definitionFit: Each combatant in an affair of honour traditionally brought an assistant, called a second, to the field.

clue.text: Give the lie to tuber that is upside down?

definitions.meaning: to show a claim is false
the word tuber written backwards is rebut, which means to refute

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: turn the letters of 'tuber' round and you get REBUT, a synonym of the answer, not a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: To prove false or refute, which is also what rebut means.

clue.text: Poor living — sixteen, roughly, going to church

indicators.note: going to tells us the church letters are added after the reworked letters
roughly says the letters of sixteen are only approximately in place and must be reordered

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A poor life spent by a teenager dragged off to services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' turns SIXTEEN into EXISTEN, and 'going to' adds CE (Church of England).
explanation.definitionFit: A bare, poor way of getting by is often called eking out a meagre being or life.

clue.text: After a breather, I find material for girders

indicators.note: after tells us the letter I comes once the breathing organ is in place

parts.note: a lung is an organ we breathe with

explanation.surface: A builder pauses for breath, then finds steel for beams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girders' are not steel beams but people who gird themselves: a LUNGI is a cloth wrapped round the waist in South Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A length of cloth wrapped around the waist in South Asia, so fabric for those who wrap themselves.

clue.text: Red-hot water-boiler, say

parts.note: seems to describe a glowing kettle, but Red means Russian and the hot-water boiler is the Russian tea urn

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as Red (Russian) hot-water boiler: the traditional Russian tea urn.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal urn traditionally used in Russia to heat water for tea.

clue.text: Who's a pretty boy, then, at university?

parts.note: taken as written
the person found at a university is a don, a college lecturer
the question 'who is?' is answered by 'is' at the end of the reply

explanation.surface: A mocking question to a vain young student about his good looks.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as a question and its reply: 'Who's at university?' gets the answer 'A don is', which run together gives the handsome youth of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this youth was loved by Aphrodite for his beauty, so his name now means any very handsome young man.

clue.text: Lay sacks in marine containers

parts.note: a lay is a short song or ballad, a ditty
sacks are bags

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' is the noun for a song, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors kept small kit such as needles and thread in these little bags.

clue.text: Traveller crazy to follow Japanese drama?

indicators.note: to follow tells us the word for crazy comes after the drama

parts.note: No (or Noh) is classical Japanese masked drama
crazy means mad

explanation.surface: A traveller goes mad trailing after a Japanese play.
explanation.walkthrough: NO (Noh) is the stylised classical drama of Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer who has no fixed home and moves from place to place.

clue.text: Legs in movement make one run

indicators.note: movement says the letters of legs in are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Moving your legs gets you one run in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is part of the fodder, not a link; 'movement' rearranges LEGSIN.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, one run scored from a stroke is called by this name.

clue.text: Capture in French bunker

parts.note: en is French for in
a sand trap is a golf bunker

explanation.surface: Trapped in a French bunker in wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: A bunker is the golf-course sand trap, not a military shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch or snare someone by a trick.

clue.text: Single issue of new coins

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of coins are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A one-off commemorative release of freshly minted money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single issue' looks like coin-collecting jargon, but issue means offspring: rearrange COINS.
explanation.definitionFit: A descendant or heir is a member of the next generation, one child of a family's line.

clue.text: Very small chaps, those old soldiers in America

parts.note: minute, said with a long u, means tiny
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Tiny fellows turn out to have been colonial American troops.
explanation.walkthrough: MINUTE here is the adjective for tiny, not the unit of time, though the soldiers took their name from being ready at a minute's notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonial militia in the American Revolutionary War were trained to turn out at very short notice, hence their name.

clue.text: Successful shot enables him to rescue the game

definitions.text: Successful shot enables him to rescue the game

parts.words: Successful shot enables him to rescue the game
parts.note: sounds like a sports hero saving a match, but the game is shot birds and he is the dog who fetches them

explanation.walkthrough: Game means birds brought down by guns, not a match; the dog fetches them once the shooter has hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun dog bred to bring back birds that a shooter has brought down.

clue.text: Effect of mountain air?

parts.note: seems to be about bracing alpine breezes, but the air is a tune sung in the mountains

explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' means a melody, not the atmosphere: Alpine herdsmen's warbling song.
explanation.definitionFit: A warbling song of Swiss and Austrian herdsmen, switching rapidly between chest voice and falsetto.

clue.text: Eg Beaujolais opening put back — owing to his delay?

parts.note: Beaujolais is an example of vin, French for wine

indicators.note: put back tells us the word for the opening is read in reverse order

parts.note: a rent is an opening such as a tear

explanation.surface: The release of a famous French red is postponed because of the wine merchant's slowness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back' turns RENT into TNER after VIN. The definition is cryptic: the person whose delay holds back the wine's release is the merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine merchant is the trader whose holding back stock would delay a new wine's release.

clue.text: Where Walther won the European Song Contest?

definitions.text: Where Walther won the European Song Contest?

parts.words: Where Walther won the European Song Contest?
parts.note: sounds like the Eurovision show, but recalls Wagner's opera The Mastersingers, where the knight Walther wins the singing contest in a German city

explanation.walkthrough: In Wagner's opera The Mastersingers, Walther von Stolzing wins the guild's song contest, set in this Bavarian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bavarian city where Wagner set his opera about a guild of master singers.

clue.text: Promote pawn first — to acclaim

indicators.note: first tells us the pawn's letter goes before the word for promote

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn
to promote someone is to raise them in rank

explanation.surface: A chess instruction: advance the pawn first, to cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess sense of 'promote' (turning a pawn into a queen) is a decoy; promote just means raise.
explanation.definitionFit: To applaud or laud someone is to express warm approval of them.

clue.text: Puffin', we hear, like Captain Flint

definitions.meaning: a puffin is a seabird with a parrot-like beak
Captain Flint is Long John Silver's parrot in Treasure Island, a bird that went to sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' points at the dropped g of Puffin' as it is spoken. Captain Flint is the parrot of Long John Silver in Treasure Island, a seafaring bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The puffin's nickname for its bright beak, and also a fitting description of a parrot that sailed with pirates.

clue.text: Tyres can burst in race

indicators.note: burst says the letters of tyres can are blown apart and come down in a new order

explanation.surface: A car's tyres may burst during a motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' is not a contest but lineage or descent.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lineage or line of descent, as in people of the same stock.

clue.text: Novel site for cricket

parts.note: suggests a new ground for the sport, but recalls Dickens's novella The Cricket on the ___, where the insect chirps by the fire

explanation.surface: A new venue for the bat-and-ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is the insect, not the British bat-and-ball game; Dickens wrote a Christmas book called The Cricket on the Hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireside floor is where house crickets traditionally chirp, as in the Dickens title.

clue.text: Dealer in ornamental clocks?

parts.note: seems to be about timepieces, but clocks are embroidered patterns on the side of a sock or stocking

explanation.walkthrough: A 'clock' is an embroidered ornament on the ankle of a sock, so the trader sells socks and stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of socks and stockings, which may bear ornamental side patterns.

clue.text: Refuse making a black mark

parts.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a stain is a mark

explanation.surface: Turning someone down leaves a black mark against you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' is the verb (decline), not rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline to vote or to hold back from something is to refuse to take part.

clue.text: Light rubber helped by powerful spirit

definitions.text: Light rubber helped by powerful spirit

parts.words: Light rubber helped by powerful spirit
parts.note: sounds like a feeble eraser and strong drink, but describes the boy who rubbed the lamp and was served by a genie

explanation.walkthrough: The 'light' is a lamp and the 'spirit' is a genie, from the Arabian Nights tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The youth in the Arabian Nights who rubs a magic lamp and summons a genie.

clue.text: Thing to end telephone conversation, we hear

definitions.meaning: a thing is a neurotic obsession, as in having a thing about spiders

explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' teases the phone listener. 'Thing' is an obsession or neurosis.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotional preoccupation, and the phrasal verb for putting the receiver down to finish a call.

clue.text: Most of egg-white is such a binder!

indicators.note: most of tells us the word for egg-white loses its tail end

parts.note: albumen is the white of an egg

explanation.surface: Egg white is mostly used in cooking to bind a mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: Egg white binds in cooking, which is the surface; but the binder is a book for stamps or photos.
explanation.definitionFit: A book with blank pages, often loose-leaf, for collecting photographs or stamps is a kind of binder.

clue.text: Trains champion couple

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the old national train operator
an ace is a champion

explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, which ran Britain's trains until the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Two game birds of the same kind, as in a pair shot together.

clue.text: Draw at Maltese resort

indicators.note: resort, read as re-sort, says the letters are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: A tie at a Mediterranean holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday place but means re-sort: rearrange ATMALTESE.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, a position where the player to move has no legal move ends the game level.

clue.text: Supernumerary 8, for example

definitions.meaning: the answer to 8 down is one run in cricket, and a run not off the bat is another kind added to the score

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, runs from byes, wides and no-balls are added to the score; the clue links this to the single run of 8 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something additional beyond what is required, and a cricket term for runs not scored off the bat.

clue.text: English port wine? The limit!

parts.note: Graves is a Bordeaux wine
the end is the limit

explanation.surface: Someone exasperated at being served port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the fortified wine but is a harbour town; GRAVESEND is a Thames port in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A town on the south bank of the Thames estuary in Kent with a long history as a harbour.

clue.text: Game pie has nothing in it

indicators.note: in it tells us the letter for nothing is placed inside the word for pie

parts.note: a tart is a pie
O is nought, nothing

explanation.surface: Disappointment at a game pie with no filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game pie' looks like one dish; 'Game' is the definition, a card game played with tarot cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game played across Europe with a special pack that includes trumps, also used for fortune telling.

clue.text: Uncle's assurance?

parts.note: seems to be a relative's promise, but Uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker, who takes goods as security

explanation.walkthrough: Uncle is old British slang for a pawnbroker; what he takes as security for a loan is also a word for a solemn promise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an item deposited as security with a pawnbroker and a solemn promise.

clue.text: Footmen with arms

parts.note: suggests liveried servants, but foot-men are soldiers who fight on foot carrying weapons

explanation.walkthrough: Footmen are not household servants here but men on foot, and arms are weapons, not limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers who march and fight on foot, carrying weapons, form this branch of an army.
